prompt: A 1990s indoor water park children's play structure, a modular multi-level play tower about 9 meters wide and 8 meters tall. Four square yellow fiberglass decks, each 2.4 m wide, on round blue steel posts, set close together in a 2x2 block at different heights: the front-left deck is low at 1.4 m, the front-right and back-left decks are at 2.6 m, the back-right deck is the highest at 3.8 m. Pointed pyramid roofs of molded plastic on three of the towers: teal green over the front-left deck, orange over the front-right deck, red over the back-left deck. The highest back-right tower has no roof: a tall rust-red painted steel frame rises from it and holds a giant faded red tipping bucket with a thick yellow rim on a horizontal steel axle about 7 m above the ground; a blue water pipe climbs a corner post of the frame and bends over the bucket. Red horizontal railing tubes with blue vertical bars along the deck edges. A straight yellow staircase with red handrails climbs from the ground at the front up to the front-left deck. Short steps link the decks. An open yellow wave slide runs down to the right from the front-right deck. Three-quarter view from the front-right, slightly from above, the whole structure visible from the floor to the top of the bucket frame. Photorealistic studio product photo of real 1990s commercial water park play equipment, very detailed and believable: fiberglass and rotomolded plastic with a slightly chalky, sun-faded and chlorine-bleached surface, powder-coated round steel posts, visible hex bolts, clamps, brackets, welded joints and rubber end caps; real wear: scuffs, fine scratches, chipped paint at the edges, limescale and dried water stains, grime in the corners and joints, a little rust bleeding from the bolts. Worn but intact and still cheerful: saturated 1990s toy colors with some faded pastel tones. Single isolated object, the whole object fully visible and centered, soft even studio lighting, plain light grey background, no people, no text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no water.
